name: Sulforaphane / broccoli sprout extract
short: Gastrointestinal side effects in a 12-week prediabetes trial; no severe adverse events. Autism trials: adverse events no more frequent than placebo. Thyroid tests unchanged in a 12-week trial.
text: In a 12-week randomised placebo-controlled trial in 74 people with prediabetes, gastrointestinal side effects, but no severe adverse events, were observed with broccoli sprout extract; the abstract does not give how often they occurred or how this compared with placebo. A meta-analysis of six randomised trials with 333 participants with autism spectrum disorder, which pooled outcomes after 4 to 5 and 8 to 10 weeks of supplementation, found no significant difference in the incidence of adverse events between sulforaphane and placebo, and a 10-week randomised trial in 60 children aged 4 to 12 given sulforaphane or placebo together with risperidone found no difference in the frequency of adverse events. A small phase I study in healthy volunteers (9 given broccoli sprout extracts and 3 placebo, every 8 hours for 7 days) observed no significant or consistent toxicities across 32 types of blood tests, including liver and thyroid tests. Because some broccoli sprout products have long been suspected of thyroid toxicity, and recent findings raise the possibility that long-term exposure to sulforaphane may lead to thyroid dysfunction or thyroid autoimmune disease, one randomised trial measured thyroid function in 45 women after 84 days of a beverage enriched with sulforaphane and its precursor and found no effect on thyroid hormones or thyroid autoimmunity. The risperidone trial is the only combination with a medicine in the cited sources; no other interaction data were found.
